summary: Decompose an objective into the candidate problems worth solving, each with the evidence that would confirm or kill it.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: The outcome you want, in one sentence. State the end, not the means — "cut onboarding drop-off", not "add a tutorial".

context.title: Context
context.description: What you already know: constraints, prior attempts, who is affected, anything that rules an answer out.

method.title: Decomposition method
method.description: How to break the objective down.

restated_objective.description: The objective restated as the analysis understood it, so a misread is visible before the problems are read.

statement.description: The candidate problem, as a falsifiable claim about the world.

why_it_matters.description: What is lost while this stays unsolved.

evidence_for.description: What is already known that supports this, drawn from the supplied context.

evidence_against.description: What would argue against it, or what is missing that should be there if it were true.

next_check.description: The cheapest observation that would confirm or kill this, and roughly what it costs.

not_the_problem.description: Plausible framings deliberately rejected, and why — so the reader can tell what was considered from what was missed.
